wording.D2_Apple_axis: DIAMETRAL clearance: 'Total Diametrical Clearance (in.)'; text 'the extrusion limit of o-rings under pressure is determined by the size of the diametrical clearance gap and the hardness of the o-ring material'.  Apple states no eccentricity convention for the chart (no 'radial' / 'eccentric' / 'concentric' in the 7 pages); its Table A [D9] limits 'Eccentricity Max.' in a separate column from 'Diametrical Clearance'.  Pressure axis: 'Fluid Pressure (psi)'.  No cycle count, duration or temperature is printed.
wording.D1_FNST_table: DIAMETRAL by definition ('Extrusion gap = Bore - Piston'), applied as the gap on ONE SIDE by its own rule: 'Unless the hardware can ensure the bore and the piston or rod remain concentric, we have to assume that all of the gap possible can shift to one side.'  The table ('Maximum Recommended Extrusion Gap', by pressure in psi) is therefore a one-side gap limit entered with the whole diametral clearance.  Scope: static, < 1500 psi.
wording.ours_0.2772: DIAMETRAL clearance: bore - piston under the FA1S step case = drawing maximum at rest 0.156 (57.25 H8 bore maximum 57.296 - 57.20 f7 plug minimum 57.140) + 2 x (case 0.0559 + plug 0.0047) radial = 0.1212.  The hardware does NOT ensure concentricity: the plug is one 57.20 f7 diameter in the 57.25 H8 bore (the gland clearance IS the fit clearance), with no separate centring feature; the ten radial screws clamp it where it was assembled.  So by [D1]'s rule the gap on one side is the full 0.2772.

passage_check.finding: the guide requires more than an edge break: the cross bores must be repositioned, chamfered internally (Fig. 2.26) or relieved by a balancing groove (Fig. 2.27, 'best'), or, at assembly, 'removed or covered' (2.5.6).  Repositioning is not possible (the glands must lie between the chamber and the holes, and TC-02 enters from the forward end).  An internal chamfer that guides a ring springing up to y into the hole would, by the lead-in rule x > y at 15-20 deg, be about 0.8 mm deep and 2.2-3.0 mm wide around a 5.5 hole in a 3.12 wall, inside the fit-contact annulus FEA3D found at the hole edge (r' 2.43-3.08): a structural change.  A balancing groove in the TC-01 bore at the screw plane would remove the fit contact there: also structural.
